newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile blue chips end weak, wineries sparkle.
newsitem.headline: Chile blue chips end weak, wineries sparkle.

text.p: Undermined by Wall Street's slide, Chilean stocks closed softer in thin turnover, although winery stocks continued their winning streak on hopes of strong sales, said traders.
Despite the fall, the underlying mood is optimistic and stocks could inch higher at the opening, they said.
"Markets are disorientated in Chile and abroad...the bolsa could open slightly firmer," said one dealer.
The 40-share index ended down 0.25 percent at 119.29 points. The general index shed 0.19 percent to 5,353.77 points on volume of 8.4 billion pesos.
Wineries resumed their rally on speculation that a free trade agreement between Chile and Canada, currently being debated in Congress, will boost sales, said dealers.
Traders said lesser known winemakers were benefitting now from the industry's bull run, which buoyed more famous brands earlier in the week.
Undurraga rose 8.11 percent to 400 pesos, while Concha y Toro was up 0.37 percent at 270 pesos.
Other winners included power utility Chilgener, which rose on the company's strong first quarter earnings, said traders.
Losers included forestry firm Masisa, down 1.67 percent at 236 pesos, with drug-maker LabChile falling 1.56 percent at 443 pesos.
